drafts.title: Keep the large, long touchscreen’s visual appeal while making core controls faster to reach, less cluttered, and resistant to visible smudging and glare
drafts.description: Customers enjoy the large, long touchscreen’s look and responsiveness but also want primary driving controls easy to find, fewer menu steps for common tasks, and a screen that stays usable in bright light and does not require frequent wiping.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a driving usability test (N=100), >=90% of participants locate and operate climate temperature, fan, audio volume and start navigation within 2 taps and 5 seconds using the primary driving view or a single dedicated ‘driver’ view; >=90% of participants report no need to wipe the active screen area during a continuous 1‑hour drive; in a daylight readability test (simulated bright sunlight) >=90% of participants correctly identify primary control icons without re-angling.
assumptions: Usability tests use a representative US driver panel (mix of new and experienced BMW drivers)
Production displays and coatings available at launch provide measurable reductions in visible fingerprints compared with current hardware
A simplified or driver-focused UI mode and customizable shortcuts will be offered as part of the default software
uncertainties: Some customers prefer deep customization and full-feature screens by default, which may conflict with a simplified driving view
Perception of glare and smudging can vary with user behavior (e.g., touching frequency) and climate

drafts.title: Ensure Apple CarPlay connects and functions reliably so iPhone owners don’t lose media, phone or navigation integration
drafts.description: Customers with iPhones should be able to pair, connect and use CarPlay without frequent disconnects or missing media; the system should consistently resume media and phone functions after connection or vehicle restart.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In lab tests across 10 popular iPhone models and iOS 16–18, CarPlay establishes a working connection and resumes media playback within 5 seconds in >=95% of connection attempts; pairing persists across vehicle restart in >=98% of attempts.
assumptions: Tested phone set includes representative models (e.g., iPhone 12–15 series) and current iOS versions at launch
Apple CarPlay protocol remains supported by Apple and phone vendors at launch
Wireless coexistence environment in test approximates real-world US conditions
uncertainties: Third‑party app behavior (Spotify, podcasts) may affect media resume behavior
Interference from other wireless devices or vehicle accessories could still cause occasional disconnects

drafts.title: Make odometer and trip mileage immediately visible and easy to access from the instrument cluster
drafts.description: Customers must be able to see current odometer and trip mileage or reach trip controls quickly and intuitively without dealer help or confusing steps.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 50‑user usability test, >=95% of participants locate current odometer and trip mileage within 5 seconds without prior training; accessing trip reset/selection requires no more than two actions.
assumptions: Instrument cluster layouts allow a default or easily reachable view for odometer/trip information
Usability panel includes both new and experienced BMW drivers
uncertainties: User personalization that hides default elements could reduce discoverability unless safeguarded
Differences between market software variants could affect the location of the mileage display

drafts.title: Deliver a wireless charging surface that reliably charges common phones and holds them flat without repeated repositioning
drafts.description: When placing a phone on the car’s wireless pad, customers expect consistent charging performance and correct fit for common phone sizes and cases, without having to wiggle the phone or plug a cable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On the production charging surface, >=90% of tested popular phones (see assumptions) charge from 20% to 80% within 75 minutes on the front pad, and >=95% of phones remain charging without repositioning during a 15‑minute normal‑road drive test.
assumptions: Test phone set includes representative devices (e.g., iPhone 12–15 series, Samsung Galaxy S20–S23/24 equivalents) with and without common thin cases
Qi wireless charging standards or widely adopted equivalents remain the de facto phone charging method at launch
uncertainties: Some phone cases, metal mounts, or third‑party accessories may prevent reliable charging
Variability across phone models and future phone designs may require updates to the pad design

drafts.title: Make voice control reliably recognize and execute common driving commands across US accents and realistic cabin noise
drafts.description: Drivers should be able to use voice to enter navigation destinations, place calls, and change climate settings with high first‑time recognition even with typical in‑car background noise.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a noise‑conditioned driving test (background noise 65–75 dB) with a participant pool representative of US accents, >=90% of voice commands for navigation entry, phone calls and climate control are correctly recognized and executed on the first attempt within 3 seconds.
assumptions: Supported command phrases for navigation, phone and climate are defined and communicated to users
Microphone array and noise suppression performance on production hardware are consistent with test conditions
uncertainties: Recognition performance may vary for less common accents, speech impediments, or heavy background music
Cloud‑based speech services may be affected by network latency if used as a fallback

drafts.title: Provide a reliable in‑car WiFi hotspot that supports several devices with consistent browsing performance on typical US routes
drafts.description: Customers expect the vehicle hotspot to deliver usable internet for multiple devices during everyday drives (commutes, errands) without frequent drops or very slow loads.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: During a 30‑minute mixed urban/suburban drive test, the vehicle hotspot supports 3 simultaneous devices with webpage load times <=5 seconds and average throughput >=10 Mbps per device in >=90% of tests, assuming an active data plan and typical carrier coverage on the test route.
assumptions: An active vehicle data plan is provisioned for the test vehicle during evaluation
Test routes reflect typical US urban/suburban cellular coverage
uncertainties: Actual performance depends on carrier network conditions, which vary by geography and time
High device counts, large downloads or streaming by passengers will reduce per‑device throughput
